# ListDetailDialog

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:list-detail-dialog` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A modal list-detail dialog whose list and detail columns each run its full height: the list column carries a secondary title and its own controls, the detail column carries the dialog's primary title, actions, and close control, and compact devices get a full-screen drill-down.

## When to use

Present a selectable list beside the selected item's detail inside a modal, with the dialog's title and close control in the detail column and a one-pane drill-down on compact devices.

- A modal task picks one record from a list and shows its detail beside it (project details, account switcher, settings categories): render ListDetailDialog with list and detail, open it with openDialog(), and pass compact from deviceClass().value.compact.
- The dialog's primary title, actions, and close control belong to the selected item's detail rather than spanning both columns, and the column divider should run the dialog's full height.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it for a single-pane dialog; use DialogSurface.
- Do not compose DialogSurface around a SplitView by hand for this layout; the surface header would span both columns and stop the divider below it.
- Do not use it when the task needs a durable route or more working space than a modal; use a page with SplitView.

**Alternatives:**

- [Surface Scaffolds](./surface-scaffold.md) (nearest) — Use DialogSurface for a single-pane dialog.
- [SplitView](./split-view.md) (responsive-alternative) — Use SplitView for the same list-detail flow as a page rather than a modal.
- [WorkbenchDialog](./workbench-dialog.md) (nearest) — Use WorkbenchDialog for an editing task with side panels.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/list-detail-dialog` — exports `ListDetailDialog`, `ListDetailDialogProps`, `ListDetailDialogList`, `ListDetailDialogDetail`, `ListDetailDialogRootAttributes`, `openDialog`, `closeDialog`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/list-detail-dialog` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/list-detail-dialog.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Wiring: `wireNavStack` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-nav-stack` (optional).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/list-detail-dialog`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuilist-detail-dialog), [`@kerfjs/ui/wire-nav-stack`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiwire-nav-stack) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- roomy modal: a full-height list column and a full-height detail column with a fixed list width (default 280px, at most 40% of the dialog)
- list column header controls and a pinned list footer
- detail header actions before the close control, a description under the title, and a pinned detail footer
- compact full-screen NavStack drill-down with the close control on every view
- definite height (default 560px) or a viewport height cap, viewport gutter, size or preferred width, and light dismiss

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [Surface Scaffolds](./surface-scaffold.md), [SplitView](./split-view.md), [NavStack](./nav-stack.md), [Pane](./pane.md), [Toolbar](./toolbar.md), [ToolbarText](./toolbar-text.md), [ToolbarControlGroup](./toolbar-control-group.md), [LucideIcon](./lucide-icon.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** open state (openDialog and closeDialog); device-class policy (compact); selected item and, on compact devices, detailActive and the back action (nav-back); list and detail content, their titles, toolbar controls, and footers; dismissal policy (lightDismiss).

**Wiring:** `wireNavStack` is optional.

**Wiring-owned state attributes** — never render, remove, or branch on these as app state:

- `data-nav-chrome-transition` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): "true" while the chrome cross-fades between the outgoing and incoming view.
- `data-nav-chrome-copy` on `kui-nav-stack__chrome-copy` (`wireNavStack`): Marks the inert, aria-hidden snapshot of the outgoing chrome shown during the cross-fade.
- `data-nav-revealed` on `kui-nav-stack__view` (`wireNavStack`): "true" on the preserved, aria-hidden previous view while an incoming view slides over it.
- `data-nav-exiting` on `kui-nav-stack__view` (`wireNavStack`): "true" on a popped view the helper briefly re-inserts to slide it out.
- `data-chrome-overlay` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): measured once the helper has measured the compact stack's overlay chrome (compactStack.chromePresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.
- `data-bottom-toolbar-overlay` on `kui-nav-stack` (`wireNavStack`): measured once the helper has measured the compact stack's overlay bottom toolbar (compactStack.bottomToolbarPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height on the stack root. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

## Geometry

Margin: parent · border: self · padding: child (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The dialog draws no header and no body inset; each column is a Pane that owns its chrome and content insets, and the column divider runs the dialog's full height.

## Accessibility

- It is a native modal \<dialog> named by label: the page is inert, focus stays inside, Escape asks to close, and focus returns to the opener on close.
- On roomy devices the detail title is a level-2 heading; every presentation keeps a close control named Close (closeLabel), and the compact back control is named by backLabel.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
